page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor architecture operating at 3.4 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. This server is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, but does not include any local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates exceptional memory performance, with both large-block read-only and write memory bandwidth placing in the top 10% tier. PassMark database operations and memory scores also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core processing is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 66283.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19664.0. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1661.0. Large-scale LLM inference represents a significant bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10% at 4.66 tokens/sec.

The E32ps_v6 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, delivering top-tier memory throughput without the added cost of bundled local NVMe storage. This makes it a cost-efficient option for deployments utilizing external premium storage. The server is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or large-scale AI model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 32-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 256.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio, with no bundled local storage or GPUs. The server exhibits top-tier memory performance, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 436.06 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 184.19 GB/sec, alongside strong database operation benchmarks. Multi-core performance is robust, though single-core metrics and large LLM inference speeds are average to poor. This profile makes the E32ps_v6 highly cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads, database management, and Redis caching, while avoiding the premium of local storage.
